risks.description: The approve endpoint answers 200/approved and its in-memory GET agrees, but the durable store is never written, so an independent re-read still sees 'pending'.
risks.basis: AC-APPROVAL-001 requires the approval to be recorded durably; the only changed file r5/fixture/app.py owns both the response and the write.

risks.description: Concurrent approves of the same invoice each apply the payment effect, so a race produces two payments for one approval.
risks.basis: AC-APPROVAL-001 says approving records THE approval (singular); r5/fixture/app.py is the mutation path.

risks.description: Because the store is persisted by rewriting the whole file, a later approval of a different invoice could drop an earlier invoice's approval, so it does not survive a re-read.
risks.basis: AC-APPROVAL-002 requires approval state to survive a re-read of persisted state.

risks.description: An approve request with no actor metadata may fail to record a durable approval at all.
risks.basis: AC-APPROVAL-001 requires an approval to be recorded durably regardless of optional request metadata.

scenarios.title: Approved response must match the durable store, not just the in-memory view
scenarios.purpose: Catch a build that reports approval (200 + in-memory GET) while never writing it to durable storage, by comparing the API view against an independent file re-read.
scenarios.rationale: The prior happy/persist scenarios gated on POST status==200, which both the ui_lies and uncertain defects can satisfy or defeat. This scenario tolerates a slow response (generous timeout) and makes the load-bearing observation the durable oracle state.py, then cross-checks it against the API's own GET so an in-memory-only 'approved' is exposed as a disagreement.
scenarios.isolation_note: Operates only on the fresh invoice id W2UI, created on first touch; no other scenario references this id, so it cannot contaminate or be contaminated. No cleanup needed because the store is per-id.
setup: Use invoice id W2UI which no other scenario touches
expected_observations: GET reflects approved in the API view
Independent durable re-read via state.py shows W2UI status=approved with exactly one approval and one payment
forbidden_observations: state.py shows W2UI status=pending while the API reported approved

scenarios.title: Two simultaneous approvals of one invoice record a single approval
scenarios.purpose: Exercise the approve path under a genuine race to ensure the durable store records exactly one approval/payment even when two requests arrive at once.
scenarios.rationale: The already-covered idempotency scenario approves twice sequentially. A concurrent double-submit is a distinct 3am worry: a check-then-act without proper guarding double-pays only under a race. The oracle is the durable payment count, not the HTTP responses, so a slow answer does not defeat the assertion.
scenarios.isolation_note: Both parallel requests and the state check address only invoice id W2CC, unique to this scenario; the in-scenario parallelism is the point and cannot leak to other scenarios because the id is not shared.
setup: Use invoice id W2CC which no other scenario touches
expected_observations: Durable re-read shows W2CC approved with approvals=1 and payments=1 despite two simultaneous approvals
forbidden_observations: state.py shows payments=2 or approvals=2 for W2CC

scenarios.title: An earlier approval survives a later approval of a different invoice on re-read
scenarios.purpose: Verify AC-APPROVAL-002 by re-reading a previously approved invoice from a fresh process after an intervening durable write, catching whole-store-rewrite regressions and never-persisted approvals.
scenarios.rationale: AC-APPROVAL-002 asks that approval state survive a re-read of persisted state. The store is saved by rewriting the entire file, so an approval of a second invoice is the natural way to stress whether an earlier invoice's approval survives. The re-read is done by an independent CLI process (state.py), not the running server's memory, which is exactly what 'survives a re-read of persisted state' means. Note: the service reseeds its store on boot, so this AC cannot be checked via a restart, only via this independent re-read.
scenarios.isolation_note: Uses two ids unique to this scenario (W2R1 approved and re-read, W2R2 the intervening write); neither is referenced elsewhere, so there is no cross-scenario contamination and no cleanup is required.
setup: Use invoice ids W2R1 and W2R2, both unique to this scenario
expected_observations: After approving W2R2, an independent re-read of W2R1 still shows status=approved with one approval and one payment
forbidden_observations: state.py shows W2R1 status=pending after the intervening approval of W2R2
W2R1 approvals or payments count is 0

scenarios.title: Approval with no actor metadata is still recorded durably
scenarios.purpose: Exercise the approve path when the optional actor field is absent to confirm a durable approval is still recorded exactly once.
scenarios.rationale: AC-APPROVAL-001 promises a durable record of approval without conditioning on request metadata. Sending an empty body checks that a missing actor neither drops nor duplicates the durable approval. Truth is read from the durable oracle so a slow response does not defeat it.
scenarios.isolation_note: Only invoice id W2MD is touched, unique to this scenario; no cleanup needed and no contamination possible.
setup: Use invoice id W2MD which no other scenario touches
expected_observations: Durable re-read shows W2MD approved with exactly one approval and one payment even though no actor was supplied
forbidden_observations: payments count other than 1 for W2MD

assumptions: state.py reads the same durable store file the approve endpoint writes, so it is a valid independent oracle for persisted state that is not fooled by an in-memory-only view.
A generous per-request timeout (15s) lets a slow-but-eventual response return, so the scenario's verdict rests on the durable state_check rather than on response latency.
Invoices are created on first touch, so each scenario can safely use a private invoice id (W2UI/W2CC/W2R1/W2R2/W2MD) with no seeding step.
The approved command 'python3 r5/fixture/state.py' accepts an invoice id as an extra argument (e.g. 'python3 r5/fixture/state.py W2UI') to scope the durable re-read.
unresolved_questions: The acceptance criteria only promise durable recording (AC-APPROVAL-001) and survival of a re-read (AC-APPROVAL-002); they do NOT promise a bounded/timely response. A build that persists the approval but then stalls past a client deadline (the 'timed out' failures seen in wave 1) satisfies both ACs while leaving the caller unable to confirm the outcome. If a response-time or definitive-answer guarantee is intended, it needs its own acceptance criterion before it can be verified — I will not invent one.

AC-APPROVAL-002 ('survives a re-read of persisted state') cannot be exercised via a service restart in this fixture because the service reseeds its store on every boot; I have therefore verified 'survives a re-read' only via an independent CLI process re-reading the file. Confirm whether restart-durability (surviving a process restart) is actually required, since that would be a stronger and currently untestable claim.

The ACs do not promise authorization or approval-actor validation, so I did not author cross_tenant/authorization scenarios. If approvals must be attributable to or gated by a specific actor, that requirement is missing from the unit.
